seats.findings: 🟠 [coupon-divisor-1000] MUST-FIX src/coupon.js:5 divides by 1000 instead of 100, so couponCents(10000, 10) returns 100 instead of 1000; the discount is one tenth of the contract value and checkoutTotal at src/checkout.js:7 inherits the error (overcharging the taxable amount and tax); change the divisor to 100

🟠 [coupon-divisor-10x] MUST-FIX src/coupon.js:5 divides by 1000 instead of 100, understating the discount 10x: couponCents(10000, 10) returns Math.round(10000*10/1000)=100 instead of 1000, and since src/checkout.js:7 computes the discount via couponCents, every checkoutTotal with pct>0 violates its contract (discount must be Math.round(subtotal*p/100), p clamped 0..100); smallest remediation is changing the divisor in src/coupon.js:5 to 100: Math.round((subtotal * p) / 100)
🟠 [invoice-format-summed] MUST-FIX src/invoice.js:5 collapses the required "amount+tax" output shape into a numeric sum: the contract's quoted template substitutes the placeholders label, amount and tax joined by a literal "+" with both figures in integer cents, so invoiceLine("Widget", 1000, 800) must return "Widget: 1000+80", but the code returns "Widget: 1080", breaking any consumer that parses the documented format; smallest remediation is `${label}: ${amount}+${taxCents(amount, rateBp)}`

🟠 [coupon-divisor] MUST-FIX src/coupon.js:5 divides by 1000 instead of 100; the spec requires Math.round(subtotal * p / 100) but the code computes Math.round((subtotal * p) / 1000), producing a discount 10× too small and corrupting checkoutTotal; change the divisor from 1000 to 100
